name: Endowment supporting a Jerusalem hospital
description: A traveller described a Jerusalem hospital in which doctors’ salaries were supported by an endowment.

impact.note: One traveller's witness of one endowed hospital; steady paid care for one city, with no known successors of this case.

date.basis: The museum catalogue dates Nasir-i Khusraw’s report to 1047.

events.statement: Nasir-i Khusraw described a hospital and endowment-supported physicians.
events.scope: The traveller’s description is accessed via a museum catalogue, not the original travel text. The patron, endowed property, beneficiaries and exact legal form are not established; no inference that it was a waqf.
events.caveats: The traveller’s description is accessed via a museum catalogue, not the original travel text. The patron, endowed property, beneficiaries and exact legal form are not established; no inference that it was a waqf.

evidence.supports: Nasir-i Khusraw described a hospital and endowment-supported physicians.

earliest_record.rationale: The museum catalogue dates Nasir-i Khusraw’s report to 1047. Earliest supported episode established here, not a claim of world priority.

caveats: The traveller’s description is accessed via a museum catalogue, not the original travel text. The patron, endowed property, beneficiaries and exact legal form are not established; no inference that it was a waqf.

research.note: Independent second reader checked the event and its cited passages, retaining the stated chronological and interpretive limits; no blanket review of other facets is implied. The cited physicians were subjects of the historical description, not contributors to the description event.
